claim: Quarantining individuals with high risk of recent infection is one of the pillars of the non-pharmaceutical interventions to control the ongoing SARS-CoV-2 pandemic.
source: Quarantining individuals with high risk of recent infection is one of the pillars of the non-pharmaceutical interventions to control the ongoing severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) pandemic (Kucharski et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kucharski et al., 2020

claim: A large fraction of transmission of SARS-CoV-2 is pre-symptomatic or asymptomatic.
source: Owing to the large fraction of transmission of SARS-CoV-2 that is pre-symptomatic or asymptomatic (Ashcroft et al., 2020; Buitrago-Garcia et al., 2020; Ferretti et al., 2020b; He et al., 2020), quarantine can prevent a substantial fraction of onward transmission that would not be detected otherwise.
evidence: Supported by multiple citations: Ashcroft et al., 2020; Buitrago-Garcia et al., 2020; Ferretti et al., 2020b; He et al., 2020

claim: Quarantine can prevent a substantial fraction of onward transmission that would not be detected otherwise.
source: Owing to the large fraction of transmission of SARS-CoV-2 that is pre-symptomatic or asymptomatic (Ashcroft et al., 2020; Buitrago-Garcia et al., 2020; Ferretti et al., 2020b; He et al., 2020), quarantine can prevent a substantial fraction of onward transmission that would not be detected otherwise.
evidence: Logical inference based on pre-symptomatic/asymptomatic transmission and supported by citations

claim: Thermal screening at airports would allow more than 50% of infected travellers to enter the general population.
source: In mathematical modelling studies, it was estimated that thermal screening at airports would allow more than 50% of infected travellers to enter the general population (Quilty et al., 2020; Gostic et al., 2020), which could have been prevented by mandatory quarantine.
evidence: Supported by citations to mathematical modelling studies: Quilty et al., 2020; Gostic et al., 2020

claim: Mandatory quarantine could have prevented more than 50% of infected travellers from entering the general population.
source: In mathematical modelling studies, it was estimated that thermal screening at airports would allow more than 50% of infected travellers to enter the general population (Quilty et al., 2020; Gostic et al., 2020), which could have been prevented by mandatory quarantine.
evidence: Inference from modelling studies cited

claim: Quarantine is a fundamental part of the test–trace–isolate–quarantine (TTIQ) intervention strategy to break chains of transmission within a community.
source: Quarantine is also a fundamental part of the test–trace–isolate–quarantine (TTIQ) intervention strategy to break chains of transmission within a community (Salathé et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Salathé et al., 2020

claim: With high or increasing case numbers, more and more people are being placed into quarantine.
source: With the high or increasing case numbers that are observed in many places around the globe, however, more and more people are being placed into quarantine.
evidence: Based on observed epidemiological trends

claim: Quarantine lowers onward transmission by preventing transmission prior to symptom onset and decreasing overall transmission from persistently asymptomatic individuals.
source: Quarantine lowers onward transmission in two ways: first, preventing transmission prior to symptom onset (with the assumption that symptomatic individuals will isolate) and decreasing overall transmission from persistently asymptomatic individuals.
evidence: Logical inference about mechanisms of quarantine effectiveness

claim: The appropriate length of quarantine depends on both incubation period and the temporal profile of infectiousness.
source: The appropriate length of quarantine thus depends on both incubation period and the temporal profile of infectiousness.
evidence: Logical inference from disease dynamics

claim: RT-PCR tests have low sensitivity in early infection.
source: In theory, quarantine periods could be avoided altogether through widespread and regular testing programmes, but the low sensitivity of reverse transcriptase PCR (RT-PCR) tests, particularly in early infection (Kucirka et al., 2020), as well as limitations on testing capacity in most countries preclude this approach.
evidence: Supported by citation to Kucirka et al., 2020

claim: Limitations on testing capacity in most countries preclude widespread and regular testing programmes as an alternative to quarantine.
source: In theory, quarantine periods could be avoided altogether through widespread and regular testing programmes, but the low sensitivity of reverse transcriptase PCR (RT-PCR) tests, particularly in early infection (Kucirka et al., 2020), as well as limitations on testing capacity in most countries preclude this approach.
evidence: Based on knowledge of testing capacity constraints

claim: Quarantine has high economic, societal, and psychological costs.
source: Quarantine has high economic, societal, and psychological costs (Nicola et al., 2020; Brooks et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Nicola et al., 2020; Brooks et al., 2020

claim: Quarantine restricts individual freedoms.
source: It restricts individual freedoms (Parmet and Sinha, 2020), although the level of restriction imposed is generally judged to be proportionate, given the severity of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19).
evidence: Supported by citation to Parmet and Sinha, 2020

claim: The level of restriction imposed by quarantine is generally judged to be proportionate, given the severity of COVID-19.
source: It restricts individual freedoms (Parmet and Sinha, 2020), although the level of restriction imposed is generally judged to be proportionate, given the severity of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19).
evidence: Based on general assessment of public health policy

claim: Individuals are generally placed into quarantine for one of two reasons: they have been identified as a recent close contact of a confirmed SARS-CoV-2 case by contact tracing, or they have returned from recent travel to an area with community transmission.
source: Individuals are generally placed into quarantine for one of two reasons: either they have been identified as a recent close contact of a confirmed SARS-CoV-2 case by contact tracing, or they have returned from recent travel to an area with community transmission that has been assessed to pose significant epidemiological risk (WHO, 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to WHO, 2020

claim: Compared with traced contacts, travel returners may have lower probability of being infected and have less precise information about the likely time of exposure.
source: These groups of quarantined individuals differ in two important ways: compared with traced contacts, travel returners may have lower probability of being infected and have less precise information about the likely time of exposure.
evidence: Logical inference about differences between quarantine groups
